observation.visible_scene: A seascape at sunset (or sunrise) shot from the shore: the sun sits low on the horizon, partly veiled by a thin horizontal cloud band, lighting the sky in a blue-to-orange-to-pink gradient beneath a large soft cloud mass overhead. A cruise-ship silhouette rests on the right-hand horizon. The foreground water shows small rolling waves and patches of white foam, with a vertical column of orange sun-reflection on the surface. The horizon line, ship, and clouds sit at the same frame positions throughout, indicating a stationary camera.
visible_changes: In the lower-left foreground, a patch of breaking-wave foam visible at the start recedes and disappears by the middle of the clip, leaving a smoother, gently rippled water surface there.
Small wave crests and foam lines across the mid- and lower-right water shift position and reshape from frame to frame, consistent with waves rolling toward the viewer.
The orange sun-reflection on the water keeps its roughly central horizontal location but its texture shimmers and deforms as the surface waves move.
The cruise ship on the horizon stays at essentially the same position relative to the horizon line, showing no detectable self-motion over the excerpt.
The overhead cloud mass, the horizon cloud band, and the sun's glow remain visually static.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the foreground foam was part of a wave that had already washed in before the clip began, or what the water looks like after the excerpt ends.
The ship's true motion and direction, which cannot be judged from a ~2.7 s window.
uncertain_details: Any very slight camera drift is not clearly distinguishable from wave motion, since the horizon and ship positions look stable.
The exact propagation direction of each individual small wave is hard to track frame-by-frame.
